To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
children from a low socioeconomic strata, with a history of poverty, had a higher amount of slow EEG waves, which is a sign of a maturational delay, than children from higher socioeconomic strata.
(1) HRC showed a maturational delay in the EEG at 4 years; (2) this maturational delay was more evident in the delta band; (3) the frontal areas showed the highest differences between the two groups.
the children in the low socioeconomic stratum had significantly more delta and theta power in their EEGs, and significantly less alpha power than children in the middle and middle-high strata.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the development of the EEG in pre-school children from a socio-cultural disadvantaged environment in Mexico.
the study of the effects of social and cultural disadvantage on the developing brain, and its possible implications for the cognitive development of the child.
the study of the effects of poverty and cultural disadvantage on cognitive development and brain maturation, and the role played by the family environment and social class in these phenomena.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HRC have more immature EEG patterns than the LRC.
there are significant differences in the power spectra of the EEG of pre-school children from low- and middle-high socioeconomic groups.
the differences found between the HRC and LRC groups are consistent with the hypothesis of a delay in brain maturation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the low socioeconomic strata children are more immature, less developed, and less able to cope with the demands of their environment than the high socioeconomic strata children.
HRC have more immature EEG patterns than LRC, and that the differences are more marked in frontal than occipital areas.
children with low socioeconomic strata have a maturational delay in brain development, which could be reflected in the EEG.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need more longitudinal studies of the effects of early life adversity on brain development.
we need to be more sensitive to the fact that children are not all born with the same opportunities and that this has an effect on their brain development.
the brain is not a fixed structure but is malleable and can be influenced by experience.
